subjectLine: China's Webworm Targets EU Govs, Microsoft Exchange Zero-Day Exploited, CISA Leak Sparks Outrage

articles.title: China's Webworm APT Uses Discord and Microsoft Graphs to Hack EU Governments
articles.summary: An advanced persistent threat group, China's Webworm, is targeting EU governments by leveraging Discord and Microsoft Graph APIs, along with SOCKS proxies. This sophisticated attack highlights nation-state capabilities and the exploitation of legitimate services for malicious purposes.

articles.title: Microsoft Exchange Zero-Day Exploited, No Patch Available
articles.summary: A critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-42897) in Microsoft Exchange is currently under active attack, with no patch yet released. This cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw allows attackers to compromise Outlook Web Access (OWA) mailboxes, posing a significant risk to organizations.

articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel, undetected for nine years, has been disclosed, allowing unprivileged local users to execute arbitrary commands as root. articles.title: Cisco Patches CVSS 10.0 Secure Workload REST API Flaw
articles.summary: Cisco has released a patch for a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-20223) in its Secure Workload product, rated at CVSS 10.0. articles.title: Microsoft Releases Mitigation for BitLocker Bypass Vulnerability 'YellowKey'
articles.summary: Microsoft has issued a mitigation for CVE-2026-45585, a zero-day vulnerability dubbed 'YellowKey' that allows for a bypass of BitLocker encryption. The vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 6.8, poses a significant risk to data security on Windows systems.

articles.title: EvilTokens Phishing Platform Bypasses MFA Using OAuth Consent
articles.summary: A new phishing-as-a-service platform called EvilTokens is successfully bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA) by exploiting OAuth consent flows. The platform has already compromised over 340 Microsoft 365 organizations, demonstrating a critical new threat to cloud security.

articles.title: MiniPlasma Windows 0-Day Grants SYSTEM Privilege Escalation
articles.summary: A new Windows zero-day vulnerability, dubbed MiniPlasma, has been disclosed, allowing attackers to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on fully patched systems. The flaw resides in the Windows Cloud Files Mini Filter Driver ('cldflt.sys').
